params.body:
## Lead and seller-rating routes act only on the dealer's own records

From the October architecture audit (#1047): a class of per-record ownership gaps. The classic
(jQuery-era) lead and seller-rating routes take the record id straight from the URL and act on the
row it names, without checking whose it is. The id is base64 of the database key (`LinkHelper::route`
encodes it, the controller decodes it), so it is guessable, not secret. The `Access` middleware only
guards the create/update/delete verbs against the role table; it does not check that a record belongs
to the logged-in dealer, and there are no policies.

This PR closes the two clearest ones.

### Leads

`LeadController::update` and `destroy` looked the lead up by `base64_decode($id)` and set `treated`
or `deleted` on it, on any dealer's lead. A logged-in user of garage A could mark garage B's leads
read, or delete them. Both routes now go through `ownLeadOrFail`: a lead that is not the dealer's own
is refused (403), one that does not exist is a 404, so the answer does not reveal which ids hold a
lead. Nothing changes for a dealer acting on its own lead.

### Seller rating (buy-over)

`storeSellerVote` wrote the rating through `Voting::addSellerVote`, whose ownership guard was
`if ($vehicle->dealer_id = Auth::user()->dealer_id)` — an assignment, not a comparison, so it was
always true. The rating is stored with the logged-in dealer as buyer but with the seller of a car it
does not own, so a dealer could rate a seller it never bought from and that rating counted in the
seller's average. This was already noted when the rating screens were rebuilt (finding
beoordeling-zonder-titel) and deferred to "a row of ownership checks".

The store route and the modal now go through `mustOwnVehicle` (same 403/404 shape as the leads), and
`Voting::addSellerVote` compares instead of assigns, as a second lock. The seller rating of a dealer's
own bought-over car is unchanged.

### Still open (named, not in this PR)

The buyer and export ratings follow a different ownership model — the seller rates the buyer (keyed on
`seller_id`), and a bid rating runs through the winning bid and the pickup release — so they get their
own checks, with their own tests, in a follow-up. Also open from the audit: the read routes
`StockListController::getRelationData` and `VehicleTextController::generate`, the `ExportController`
PDFs, and the broad filter-key allowlist in `VehicleRepository::extendedSearch`.

### Tests

`LeadAndSellerVoteOwnershipTest` drives the routes with `withoutMiddleware()` (so it exercises the
controller's own check, not the role seeding): a lead and a rating of another garage return 403 and
leave the row untouched; the own lead and own car still work; the own rating is written with the
logged-in dealer as buyer and the right seller. The four refusal cases fail on main; the two
own-record cases already pass.

Business rules R P1-3.11 (leads) and R S5-3.13 (seller rating) carry the ownership behaviour and the
sources, with the finding een-lead-of-een-beoordeling-raakte-elke-garage. The singleshowroom finding's
`opgelost_in` is corrected from #1049 to #1050 (the PR that actually merged).

PHPStan clean; full suite green.
params.title: Lead and seller-rating routes act only on the dealer's own records
